// ======== KOBITON CLI ========

// Source: KOB-52718 from PR #743

== Kobiton CLI: Session Explorer for CLI sessions

- Added the `--capture` option to `kobiton session create`. List the session data to capture, such as `screenshots`, `view-trees`, `logs`, `metrics`, or `video`, and review it in Session Explorer. Capture is opt-in. CLI sessions created without `--capture` capture no session data and continue to open on Session Overview.

// Source: KOB-55503 from PR #738

=== Accurate per-step device logs for Kobiton CLI sessions

- Fixed an issue where per-step device logs for Kobiton CLI sessions appeared under the wrong step or were empty. Each step now shows the device log lines recorded since the previous step, and the first step shows the lines recorded before it.

// Source: KOB-55494 from PR #734

=== Session Overview

- Fixed an issue where *View Device Logs* showed a `Failed to download log content` error for sessions that captured no device logs, such as Kobiton CLI sessions created without `logs` in the capture list. For these sessions, *View Device Logs* is now disabled, and its tooltip says "No device logs were captured for this session". *Download all* is also disabled when the session captured no logs at all. Sessions with device logs are unchanged.

// Source: KOB-55504 from PR #735

=== Fewer duplicate steps in Kobiton CLI session timelines

The Session Explorer timeline for Kobiton CLI sessions no longer shows an extra `POST /session` step for every `kobiton webdriver` call. The timeline now shows the session creation once, followed by one step for each call.

* Repeated session creation requests are hidden from the timeline but remain in the session's command data.
* A failed session creation request still appears as a step.
* The device logs for each call include the log lines since the previous call.
* CLI sessions recorded before this change display the same way.

Automation and mixed sessions are not affected.

// Source: KOB-55505 from PR #736

=== Kobiton CLI: Screenshots in Session Explorer

- Steps in CLI sessions that do not have their own screenshot now show the screenshot from the previous step, as automation sessions do. Previously, these steps showed "Screenshot Not Available". This applies in Session Explorer and in the session command APIs.
- The XML hierarchy in *Appium Inspector* follows the same rule. *Appium Inspector* never pairs a screenshot with the XML hierarchy from an earlier step.

// ======== SESSION EXPLORER ========

// Source: KOB-55471 from PR #737

== Session Explorer

- Fixed an issue where sessions with no recorded steps opened on an empty Session Explorer. These sessions now open on *Session Overview*, and the *Explorer* tab shows _Explorer is not available for this session_. Sessions with recorded steps still open on Session Explorer.

// Source: KOB-55496 from PR #744

* Bug Fix: Fixed an issue where XCUITest sessions that ran tests showed Session Explorer steps labeled `null` with no screenshots. These sessions now open on *Overview*, and the *Explorer* tab shows "Explorer is not available for this session." Sessions with recorded steps are not affected.

// Source: KOB-55400 from PR #724

== Crash logs

- Session Explorer again shows app crashes and their crash logs for sessions on Android and iOS devices. This applies to manual, Appium, and API sessions. Previously, an app crash during a session was not captured, and no crash log was available for the session.

// ======== MANUAL TESTING ENTRIES ========

// Source: KOB-55419 from PR #753

== Manual testing

- Fixed an issue where app installation errors in manual sessions hid the error reported by the device. For some iOS and Android errors, Kobiton Portal replaced the device error with its own explanation, which could point to the wrong cause. The error message now shows the device error text after `Failed to install '<app>'.`, for example `ApplicationVerificationFailed`, `INSTALL_FAILED_VERSION_DOWNGRADE`, `INSTALL_FAILED_UPDATE_INCOMPATIBLE`, `INSTALL_FAILED_OLDER_SDK`, or `DeviceOSVersionTooLow`. When an install error includes a Kobiton error code, the code still appears at the start of the message.
- iOS installs that fail signature verification now show the `ApplicationVerificationFailed` error instead of an AS-500 message stating that *App signing using Kobiton Certificate (iOS)* is disabled. This error means the app's own signature isn't valid on the device, for example, because the provisioning profile doesn't include the device UDID or the profile or certificate has expired.

// Source: KOB-53003 from PR #709 (broader scope)
// Source: KOB-53785 from PR #708 (earlier Apple Pay-scoped entry; merged here)

== Passcode entry in iOS manual sessions

Enter the device passcode on iOS system passcode screens during a manual session. These screens appear for Apple Pay, the Wallet *Add Card* flow, and the hidden apps folder. iOS hides the keypad from the session video stream, so Kobiton Portal displays a tappable overlay.

* A numeric keypad overlay appears on the session stream when the passcode screen is detected. Tap the overlay to enter the passcode. Entry progress shows as dots, and the digits are never displayed.
* Select *Auto-fill passcode* to enter the device's configured passcode.
* Use the *Passcode helper* menu on the session toolbar to show or hide the keypad overlay and to auto-fill the passcode.
* The passcode helper supports iPhone screen sizes, portrait and landscape orientation, and Display Zoom.

Available in manual sessions only. For Apple Pay steps, see xref:manual-testing:local-devices/use-apple-pay-in-manual-session.adoc[Use Apple Pay on iOS devices].

// Source: KOB-53003 from PR #709 (Passcode support on Devices page)
// Source: KOB-53007 from PR #707 (earlier Passcode filter entry; merged here)

== Passcode support on the Devices page

Identify devices ready for passcode entry on the Devices page.

* Filter the device list by *Passcode*, with *Supported* or *Not Supported* values, in the device search bar alongside criteria such as Operating System and Audio.
* A passcode icon next to the device name in card view and list view marks devices ready for passcode entry. Hover over the icon to show *Passcode enabled - required for Apple Pay*.

A device is *Supported* when your organization has passcode (PIN) mode turned on and the device has a passcode set.

// ======== AUTOMATION TESTING ENTRIES ========

// Source: KOB-54326 from PR #722 (organization settings UI)
// Source: KOB-55121 from PR #723 (session behavior; shipped with KOB-54326)

== Appium AI organization settings

Administrators can now configure Appium AI for the whole organization in Kobiton Portal. New Appium sessions use the organization's LLM provider and locator settings — endpoint, models, and API key — without extra capabilities in test scripts.

*Highlights*

* Turn Appium AI on or off for the organization. When Appium AI is off, natural language finds fail with the error `LLM client is disabled for this organization`, and session capabilities cannot turn it back on.
* Set the default LLM endpoint, API key, API format, text and vision models, extra request body, locator strategy, and coordinate space.
* Require an API key whenever an LLM endpoint is set, except for the Ollama chat API format.
* Apply saved settings to new sessions on every device host in the organization. Running sessions keep their current settings.
* Override organization settings for a single session with `kobiton:*` desired capabilities. Session capabilities take precedence field by field. Organizations without LLM settings continue to use the host defaults.

For details, see xref:automation-testing:appium-ai/configure-appium-ai-org-settings.adoc[Configure Appium AI settings for your organization].

// Source: KOB-55464 from PR #746 (iOS 26 location permission alert)
// Source: KOB-55472 from PR #739 (XCUITest session details 500 error)
// Source: KOB-54432 from PR #713 (iPad Appium Inspector hierarchy)

// Source: KOB-55355 from PR #728 (Inspector XML hierarchy on Android 13+ web views)

== Appium automation

- Fixed an issue where, on iOS 26, Appium automation scripts could not find the buttons on the location permission alert, such as *Allow Once*, *Allow While Using App*, and *Don't Allow*. The page source now includes the alert and its buttons, so scripts can locate them and accept or dismiss the alert. Previously, the page source sometimes showed only the map inside the alert, and scripts failed with a `no such element` error.
- *Session details for running XCUITest sessions:* Fixed an issue where session details failed to load while an XCUITest native framework session was still running. During the run, `+GET /v1/sessions/{id}+` and `+GET /v2/sessions/{id}+` returned an HTTP 500 error. Both now return the session at every stage of the run, including before its test report and video are available. Finished sessions with a recorded video keep their video link.
- Fixed an issue where *Appium Inspector* in Session Explorer showed the same XML hierarchy for every step of an iPad automation session started without an app, such as a web session in Safari. *Appium Inspector* now shows the hierarchy for each step of these sessions, as it already does on iPhone and Android devices. iPad automation sessions that install an app, and manual sessions on iPad, are unchanged.
- Fixed an issue on Android 13 and later where the Inspector did not display the XML hierarchy for some screens that contain a web view. Element searches on these screens also failed in manual sessions and automation scripts. The Inspector now loads the full XML hierarchy for these screens, and scripts can find and interact with their elements.
- Fixed an issue where requesting an attribute that an element doesn't have, such as `value`, returned an error in Android native app sessions. The WebDriver Get Element Attribute command now returns `null` for an absent attribute, as the W3C WebDriver specification requires, and the session remains usable. Known attributes such as `text`, `enabled`, and `checked` still return their values, and requests for a stale element still return an error.

// ======== KOBITON MCP SERVER ========

// Source: KOB-55265 from PR #721

== Kobiton MCP server

AI assistants connected to the Kobiton MCP server can now tell whether a session's validation scans have finished. Previously, a scan that was still running returned the same empty result as a finished scan with no findings. The server now reports progress for accessibility, crash, response time, and network payload scans, along with a pending count for crash logs still being processed, so an assistant can distinguish results that are still arriving from final ones.

Device list responses also signal when they are truncated. The server reports the total number of matching devices alongside the limit it applied, so an assistant can narrow its search by platform, device name, UDID, or device group when results don't fit.

List endpoints now cap page sizes to keep responses within an AI assistant's context limits. Test cases, test suites, and test runs return at most 20 items per page with a default of 10, and user input events default to 10 per call. The full count stays available so an assistant can page through larger result sets.

For details, see xref:ai:mcp/ai-plugin-mcp-ref.adoc[Kobiton AI plugin and tools reference].

// ======== KOBITON API ========

// Source: KOB-55322 from PR #726

== Reset stuck device states with the Kobiton API

Org admins can now use the Kobiton API to reset devices whose state is stuck on the wrong value, such as a device that still shows as in use after its session has ended.

The new `POST /v2/execute-admin-tasks` endpoint runs predefined admin tasks. The first available task, `RESET_DEVICE_STATE`, accepts a list of device UDIDs and resets the state of each device to the default state.

* Returns the previous state and new state for each device, plus a summary of how many devices were reset, unchanged, or failed.
* Processes each device independently. If one device fails, the other devices in the request are still processed.
* Changes only the device state recorded in Kobiton. The task does not send commands to the device or its host machine, and it does not end sessions or cancel reservations.
* Limits org admins to devices in their own organization. Available for Cloud and Standalone.

After a reset, the device becomes available for sessions the next time its host machine reports on the device.

// Source: KOB-55366 from PR #710

== List the apps installed on a device with the API

* New API endpoints return the apps installed on a private device, including apps installed outside your app repository, such as through MDM or manually:
** `+GET /v2/devices/{deviceId}/installed-apps+`
** `+GET /v2/devices/udid/{udid}/installed-apps+`
* Each app in the response includes its bundle ID, name, version, and build version. On Android devices, the app name is empty.
* To include the app repository version ID for apps that match a version in your app repository, add `includeKobitonAppVersionId=true` to the request.
* The `type` parameter accepts `user`, `system`, `all`, `filesharing`, `enabled`, and `disabled`. Currently, the endpoints return every app on the device, including system apps, and the `type_applied` response field reports the filter that was applied.
* If the device is offline or does not respond, the endpoints return an error that describes the problem.
* `+GET /v2/devices/{deviceId}/apps+` is unchanged and continues to return only apps that are in your app repository.

== Fold and unfold foldable devices in manual sessions

Manual sessions on foldable Android devices, such as Galaxy Z Fold and Pixel Fold, now include a fold control in the session toolbar, and Session Explorer records each fold or unfold as a timeline step.

*Session toolbar*

* The fold control appears above *Rotate Screen* on foldable devices and shows the action it performs next: *Fold device* or *Unfold device*.
* The session starts in the device's physical posture.
* After a fold or unfold, the device screen and *Inspector* switch to the size and shape of the active screen.

*Session Explorer*

* Each fold or unfold appears on the timeline as a *FOLD DEVICE* or *UNFOLD DEVICE* step, with its own icon and screenshot.
* Screenshots keep the screen size and shape of the posture the device was in, instead of being stretched or cropped.
* Touch and swipe markers line up with the screenshot they belong to.

Flip-style foldable devices, such as Galaxy Z Flip, are not supported.

For details, see xref:manual-testing:device-controls.adoc#_fold_or_unfold_device[Device controls] and xref:session-explorer:analytics/use-the-session-timeline.adoc#_review_fold_and_unfold_steps[Review fold and unfold steps].

// Source: KOB-55444 from PR #699

== iOS device connection

- deviceConnect now reliably mounts the Developer Disk Image (DDI) on newer iOS devices, such as iPhone 18 models running iOS 26.4 and later. Previously, the DDI mount could fail intermittently, or fail when a DDI was already mounted on the device.

// Source: KOB-50523 from PR #694

== Device cleanup on iOS and iPadOS

- Device cleanup on iOS and iPadOS now resets settings such as time zone, language, and HTTP proxy on devices with the newer Settings layout. Previously, layout changes in newer iOS and iPadOS releases could cause these cleanup steps to fail with an `Error while cleaning up device, cleanup steps failed` message.

// Source: KOB-55245 from PR #651

== iOS device health checks and passcode mode

- When the XCTest runner fails to start on an iOS device, the device health check now reports the runner error, such as `Failed to load the test bundle`. Previously, deviceConnect attempted to clear the device passcode first, and a passcode error such as `Missing organization certificate` replaced the runner error.
- deviceConnect no longer removes a device passcode when a runner failure is unrelated to the passcode. The device keeps its passcode.
- In organizations that use passcode mode, deviceConnect no longer sets a passcode on an iOS device that is not supervised by the organization. The device health check fails with `Cannot set passcode: the device is not supervised by this organization.`, and the device stays unavailable until it is supervised or passcode mode is turned off. A session that requests a passcode on such a device fails at setup.

// Source: KOB-55369 from PR #674

== deviceConnect

- Fixed an issue where deviceConnect on macOS listed a device that did not exist when the host used a Cambrionix PowerPad15S hub and a HarmonyOS `hdc` server was running on the host. The extra device used the hub's USB-serial control port as its identifier, such as `/dev/cu.usbserial-<hub-serial>`, and appeared in the device lists in deviceConnect and Kobiton Portal as *Online* with a connectivity error. The hub, its ports, and the devices connected to it continue to work as before.

== Wait For Deployment (10/15)

// Source: KOB-55461 from PR #725

=== Turbo Test Execution test reports

Fixed an issue where some Turbo Test Execution sessions completed successfully but did not show a *Test Report* in Kobiton Portal, and the session API did not return a test report download URL. Test reports for these sessions are now linked to the session when it starts and are available after the session completes.

For details on downloading test reports, see xref:automation-testing:turbo-test-execution/run-appium-test.adoc#_download_test_report[Download test report].
